sentences.text: The genus is defined by specimen YPM 2195, a partial skeleton that includes the torso, back vertebrae, ribs, gastralia, shoulder girdle, humeri, forearm, and hand.
This animal differs from similar contemporaneous basal sauropodomorphs like Thecodontosaurus and Pantydraco in the specific structure of its humerus.
According to Gregory S. Paul, Asylosaurus measured 2 meters in length and weighed approximately 250 kilograms.
Partial remains were discovered in the autumn of 1834 and initially described in 1836 by Henry Riley and Samuel Stutchbury as belonging to Thecodontosaurus.

The remains were brought to Yale University by Othniel Charles Marsh between 1888 and 1890, allowing them to survive a 1940 World War II bombardment that destroyed the original holotype of Thecodontosaurus.
Asylosaurus was formally described as a distinct genus in 2007 by Peter Galton.
The type species is named A. yalensis, which refers to Yale University.
The fossils originated from a Rhaetian-age cave fill at Durdham Down in Clifton, Bristol.
Researchers suggest Asylosaurus may have occupied a separate ecological niche from related animals based on whether it was omnivorous or herbivorous.
Asylosaurus belongs to the parent group Sauropodomorpha.
It is classified within the class Saurischia.
Asylosaurus lived during the Rhaetian stage, between 205.7 and 201.4 million years ago.
